A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original controlled CLIP training experiments, generalization measurements, and representation and circuit analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds model-specific similarity analyses and neuron-threshold sensitivity results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The CLIP training procedure, SAE analysis, circuit discovery, and similarity methods are retained, including Algorithms 1–2. Testing additional neuron thresholds does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-Captions, CC3M, CC12M, DomainNet, and ImageNet-Sketch for the same domain and compositional generalization tasks. The added analyses examine existing data and training scenarios.

E2.justification: The supervised ResNet-50 comparisons and CLIP/SigLIP/BLIP comparison membership remain unchanged, including Tables 9, 10, and 12. The added analyses introduce no new comparator method.

E3.justification: Figure 21 adds an evaluation protocol that varies neuron-retention thresholds and averages Jaccard scores across layers on unseen classes C2. Existing training settings, splits, classification metrics, and the default 10% neuron-retention setting are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C extends the existing CKA, neuron-sharing, and circuit-similarity analyses from the domain-invariant-caption model to the five existing CG high-diversity models. Figures 18, 20, and 21 and Table 14 provide focused checks of consistency across models and neuron thresholds.

E5.justification: The three-run/three-seed disclosures and existing uncertainty displays are retained. The added analyses introduce no new run-count disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test.

E6.justification: v3 adds CKA, Jaccard, and threshold-sensitivity results plus Table 14, which reports Quickdraw circuit similarities of 0.176 for test-domain versus others and 0.272 for others versus others. Figure 6c also changes the existing 'Others' value from 0.268 to 0.28. Classification results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 and the mathematical definitions and derivations in Equations 1–12 are retained. Relocation and notation spacing do not change their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about domain diversity, possible compositional-generalization failures, and shared representations and circuits. The added evidence supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving class overlap and insufficient feature/circuit sharing remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning dataset scale, quality, and graph-kernel false positives. The new appendix observations support the existing interpretation without adding a new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix C clarifies which caption-controlled model produced the retained similarity results. Section C.3 newly details averaging circuit similarities across classes and non-Quickdraw domains. These are documentation additions; training hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning of mechanistic similarity relative to prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds localized explanatory and results paragraphs in Appendix C, corrects minor wording, and changes internal references from 'Appendix' to 'Section'. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix C adds three multi-panel figures and Table 14, expands captions, and rearranges existing displays. Figures 16–17 are grouped together, and v2 Figure 18 becomes v3 Figure 19 with unchanged plotted content. The overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: v3 checks the existing mechanistic findings across the original CG high-diversity models and neuron-retention thresholds, reducing dependence on the single caption-controlled model emphasized in v2. Together with clearer model attribution and aggregation details, these focused additions modestly strengthen evidential support and reproducibility.
